nodes.label: Finding: escalation logic misses zero-result-without-block case
nodes.rationale: orchestrator.py's _apply_escalation only handles the clinical+blocked partial-evidence case; when a requested domain returns zero results without being blocked while another domain succeeds, the response returns as 'answered' instead of 'insufficient_evidence', silently dropping an entire half of a multi-domain question while showing a fully-confident green banner — contradicting escalation-rules.md row 2.

nodes.label: Finding: missing CORS middleware
nodes.rationale: main.py configures no CORS middleware, so the shipped frontend (served separately) cannot call the shipped backend cross-origin: POST /query's JSON content-type triggers a CORS preflight that fails without Access-Control-Allow-Origin, causing fetch() to throw even though the backend is reachable at the network layer.

nodes.label: Finding: confidence heuristic counts URLs not distinct sources
nodes.rationale: grounding.py's corroboration-count heuristic counts distinct citation URLs, not distinct sources/hosts, so multiple hits from one client can inflate confidence to 'high' even though all citations are from a single host — contradicting the module docstring's 'independent allowlisted sources agreeing' semantics, and this inflated confidence can be the deciding factor in whether escalation triggers.

nodes.label: Finding: reload_allowlist() never called, stale lru_cache
nodes.rationale: allowlist.py's reload_allowlist() exists to pick up a human-approved edit to sources.json but is never called anywhere; a running backend keeps serving a stale lru_cache'd allowlist, so a newly-approved host keeps raising AllowlistError until the process restarts, breaking the promised 'zero-code-change activation'.

nodes.label: Finding: dead-code re-validation in /query, real error path uncaught
nodes.rationale: main.py's belt-and-suspenders re-validation in /query is dead code because orchestrator.run_query() already validates and raises before returning; the real SchemaValidationError path propagates uncaught from an unguarded call site, producing a generic unhandled-exception 500 instead of the intended HTTPException(500) with schema-error detail.

nodes.label: Finding: server filesystem path leaks via escalation.reason
nodes.rationale: AllowlistError messages embed the absolute server filesystem path (ALLOWLIST_PATH) and the full allowed-hosts list; these strings flow verbatim into escalation.reason returned by the API and rendered in the UI, leaking the server's absolute directory path (including local username) to any end user who triggers escalation on a blocked source.

nodes.label: Finding: javascript: URI XSS via unescaped citation href
nodes.rationale: frontend/app.js's escapeAttr() only escapes double quotes before a citation URL is interpolated into an href attribute, so a javascript: URI citation is rendered as a live clickable link rather than neutralized; clicking such a citation link would execute attacker script in the page's origin.

nodes.label: Finding: unauthenticated provider-key endpoint, unrestricted file perms
nodes.rationale: POST /settings/provider-key has no authentication and stores the raw provider API key to disk without restrictive file permissions; any local process/user on a shared host can read another session's plaintext key, and any network client reaching the backend can overwrite the stored key for all users of that backend instance.

nodes.label: Finding: frontend and backend both default to port 8000
nodes.rationale: frontend/README.md's suggested launch command (python3 -m http.server, default port 8000) and backend's default uvicorn invocation (no --port given, defaults to 8000) collide; whichever starts second fails to bind the port, and app.js's default API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000 ends up pointed at whichever server won the port.
